brief: Model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (3) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 300 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.6 mm pitch.

(2) Add a 96 × 96 mm square pad, 96 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. Like a tip: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. Like a key fob: model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (3) Cut a Ø130 mm hole, 400 mm deep, in the top face 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 190 mm pitch.

Model a flat 2400 × 1600 mm sheet of thickness 6 mm, centred on the origin. (3) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 0.05 mm down the side and 0.1 mm across the face.

Like a paddle: model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Add a 150 × 150 mm square pad, 150 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (3) Cut a Ø130 mm hole, 400 mm deep, in the top face 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 190 mm pitch.

Like a finial: model a sphere of Ø2400 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 720 mm, leaving a flat of Ø1920 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Add two Ø230 mm cylinders, 230 mm tall, standing on the flat cap face with centres 768 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X and exactly 230 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (3) Cut a Ø190 mm hole, 770 mm deep, in the flat cap face 768 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 290 mm pitch.

Like a donut: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (2) Add a Ø12 mm boss, 14 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M12 × 1.75 external thread over its full length, with a 1.75 mm chamfer at the tip.

Model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Add a Ø150 mm boss, 150 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1125 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Cut a Ø130 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 400 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 190 mm pitch (centred on the hole). (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 64 mm.

Model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 4.8 × 4.8 mm square pad, 4.8 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Cut a Ø4 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 16 mm deep. (3) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the top face 16 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a pebble: model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Cut a Ø150 mm notch, 500 mm deep, centred exactly on the outer edge of the top face at the point where the periodic spline closes (the +X point), so it straddles the seam. (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 64 mm down the side and 128 mm across the face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 64 mm.

Like a pin: model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 140 × 140 mm square pad, 140 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 480 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 84 mm radius.

Like a paddle: model a 25 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (30, 0), (22.7, 15.1), (0, 18), (-22.7, 15.1), (-30, 0), (-19.7, -13.1), (-0, -22), (19.7, -13.1)]. (1) Hollow the body to 1.9 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add two Ø3.8 mm cylinders, 3.8 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 26.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and exactly 3.8 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (3) Extrude a Ø3.2 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 10 mm to add a boss.

Like a tip: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø50 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø20 mm at the top, 50 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø2 mm hole, 8 mm deep, in the top face 8 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 3 mm pitch. (2) Add a Ø2.4 mm boss, 2.4 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 8.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (3) Add a 2 × 2 mm square boss, 8 mm tall, centred 3 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. (1) Add a 96 × 96 mm square pad, 96 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 320 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Cut a Ø80 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 320 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 120 mm pitch (centred on the hole).

Model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Cut a Ø130 mm hole, 400 mm deep, in the top face 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 190 mm pitch. (2) Drill a Ø150 mm blind hole, 500 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 1124.95 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.05 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 90 mm radius.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 0.072 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add two Ø0.14 mm cylinders, 0.14 mm tall, standing on the flat cut face with centres 0.48 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward +X and exactly 0.14 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (3) Split the body with the plane Z = 0.3 mm into two bodies and keep both.

Like a handle: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a Ø0.12 mm boss, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.44 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.4 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch (centred on the hole).

Model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Cut a 0.48 × 0.48 mm square notch, 0.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.4 mm deep. (3) Hollow the body to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a cam: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Add two Ø0.48 mm cylinders, 0.48 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 300 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and exactly 0.48 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 0.2 mm down the side and 0.4 mm across the face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm.

Like a nozzle: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Add two Ø0.24 mm cylinders, 0.24 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 0.8 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and exactly 0.24 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (2) Extrude a Ø0.2 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 0.8 mm to add a boss. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.1 mm.
Like a bookend: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. Split the body with the plane Z = 500 mm into two bodies and keep both.

Model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.15 mm. (2) Add a separate Ø0.36 mm cylinder body, 0.36 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.3 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Add a 0.3 × 0.3 mm square boss, 0.8 mm tall, centred 0.45 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre.

Like a bookend: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø160 mm hole, 400 mm deep, in the top face 1040 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 240 mm pitch. (2) Drill a Ø190 mm blind hole, 500 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 1104.95 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.05 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Hollow the body to 80 mm walls, removing the top face.

Model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a separate Ø0.36 mm cylinder body, 0.36 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.3 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Add a Ø1.6 mm boss, 1.6 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M1.6 × 0.35 external thread over its full length, with a 0.35 mm chamfer at the tip. (3) Hollow the body to 0.18 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Like a dome cover: model a sphere of Ø4 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 1.2 mm, leaving a flat of Ø3.2 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Cut a Ø0.32 mm hole, 1.3 mm deep, in the flat cap face 1.28 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.48 mm pitch. (2) Drill a Ø0.38 mm blind hole, 1.6 mm deep, in the flat cap face with its centre 1.4 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so only a 0.01 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Sketch a 0.13 × 0.13 mm square whose centre is 0.48 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the flat cap face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the flat cap face.

Model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø140 mm boss, 140 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 530 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Sketch a 48 × 48 mm square whose centre is 180 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face.

Like a shim: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a 190 × 190 mm square notch, 500 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Add a 160 × 160 mm square boss, 400 mm tall, centred 240 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre.

Like a spacer: model a Ø3 × 4 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.15 mm. (2) Add a Ø0.36 mm boss, 0.36 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1.32 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (3) Hollow the body to 0.15 mm walls, removing the top face.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Sweep a Ø0.1 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 0.3 mm that leaves the centre of the top face going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube. (2) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch.

Model a Ø3 × 4 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a 0.36 × 0.36 mm square notch, 1.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Cut a Ø0.3 mm hole 1.2 mm deep, centred 0.45 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a Ø0.12 mm boss, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.44 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (3) Sweep a Ø0.1 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 0.3 mm that leaves the centre of the top face going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube.

Like a base plate: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a Ø0.48 mm boss, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 499.76 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 0.28 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 0.56 mm at the opposite point.

Like a panel: model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a 0.36 × 0.36 mm square notch, 1 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 0.15 mm down the side and 0.3 mm across the face. (3) Hollow the body to 0.18 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø50 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø20 mm at the top, 50 mm tall. (1) Hollow the body to 1.2 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a 2.4 × 2.4 mm square pad, 2.4 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Offset the top face outward by 8 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected).

Like a lamp shade: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø50 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø20 mm at the top, 50 mm tall. (1) Add a 2.4 × 2.4 mm square pad, 2.4 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Draft all side faces by 3°, with the bottom face as the neutral plane, so the body narrows toward the top face.

Like a shim: model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 2 mm. (2) Drill a Ø4.8 mm blind hole, 12.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 27.58 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.02 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Cut a Ø4 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 10 mm deep.

Like a ring: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.8 mm. (2) Add two Ø1.9 mm cylinders, 1.9 mm tall, standing on the flat cut face with centres 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward +X and exactly 1.9 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (3) Hollow the body to 0.8 mm walls, removing the flat cut face.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Make a separate Ø0.2 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body. (3) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø0.12 mm notch, 0.5 mm deep, centred exactly on the outer edge of the top face at the cone's 0° seam line (at +X), so it straddles the seam. (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 0.05 mm down the side and 0.1 mm across the face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.05 mm.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a guitar pick: model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Cut a Ø0.29 mm notch, 1 mm deep, centred exactly on the outer edge of the top face at the point where the periodic spline closes (the +X point), so it straddles the seam. (2) Cut a Ø0.24 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.8 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.36 mm pitch (centred on the hole). (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.12 mm.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.06 mm. (2) Drill a Ø0.14 mm blind hole, 0.3 mm deep, in the flat cut face with its centre 0.52 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so only a 0.01 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Sketch a 0.048 × 0.048 mm square whose centre is 0.18 mm from the vertical axis through the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0), and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the flat cut face.

Like a peg: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a separate Ø0.12 mm cylinder body, 0.12 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.1 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Split the body with the plane Z = 500 mm into two bodies and keep both. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch.

Model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 300 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.6 mm pitch. (2) Add a separate Ø0.48 mm cylinder body, 0.48 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Hollow the body to 0.2 mm walls, removing the top face.

Model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm. (2) Add a 0.48 × 0.48 mm square pad, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole 0.4 mm deep, centred 0.6 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis.

Like a traffic cone: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole, 0.4 mm deep, in the top face 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch. (2) Add a separate Ø0.12 mm cylinder body, 0.12 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.1 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.4 mm deep.

Like a label plate: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 0.48 × 0.48 mm square pad, 0.48 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the top face with an unequal chamfer, 0.2 mm down the side and 0.4 mm across the face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm.

Model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Add a separate Ø0.48 mm cylinder body, 0.48 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole 0.4 mm deep at the centre of the top face, then repeat it 4 times, 0.6 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the top face that curves toward +Y with a 2.4 mm radius. (3) Hollow the body to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 40 mm. (2) Add a separate Ø96 mm cylinder body, 96 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 80 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Split the body with the plane Z = 1000 mm into two bodies and keep both.

Like a bushing: model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square notch, 0.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Loft a neck 0.4 mm tall from a 0.1 × 0.1 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.1 mm circle on a plane 0.4 mm above it.

Like a bookend: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm. (2) Drill a Ø0.48 mm blind hole, 0.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 499.755 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.005 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Make a separate Ø0.8 mm cylinder, 3.2 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 0.2 mm below the top face at the centre of the top face, and subtract it from the body.

Model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 4.8 × 4.8 mm square pad, 4.8 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Offset the top face outward by 16 mm (move the face along its normal, keeping the side faces connected).

Like a bracket: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. Sketch a 0.16 × 0.16 mm square whose centre is 0.6 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face.

Like a bookend: model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Drill a Ø4.8 mm blind hole, 12.5 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 27.58 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.02 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 2.8 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 5.6 mm at the opposite point. (3) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 10 mm deep, in the top face 26 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch.

Like a donut: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Cut a Ø0.1 mm hole at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 500 mm, Y = 0), 0.2 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.15 mm pitch (centred on the hole).

Like a pebble: model a flat sheet of thickness 0.2 mm with a closed spline outline (see below), centred on the origin [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Cut a 0.096 × 0.096 mm square notch, 0.1 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (1) Cut a Ø0.14 mm notch, 0.3 mm deep, centred exactly on the outer edge of the flat cut face at the torus's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so it straddles the seam. (2) Split the body with the plane Z = 0.3 mm into two bodies and keep both.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø96 mm boss, 96 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 352 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1500 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Chamfer both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with an unequal chamfer, 40 mm down the side and 80 mm across the face. (3) Hollow the body to 48 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Add a separate Ø4.8 mm cylinder body, 4.8 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Add a 4 × 4 mm square boss, 16 mm tall, centred 6 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre.

Model a Ø1 × 1000 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 0.06 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add two Ø0.12 mm cylinders, 0.12 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and exactly 0.12 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a constant 0.07 mm radius.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add a 0.14 × 0.14 mm square pad, 0.14 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (2) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with a constant 0.084 mm radius. (3) Cut a Ø0.12 mm hole, 0.24 mm deep, in the flat cut face 0.48 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.18 mm pitch.

(3) Extrude a Ø0.24 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 0.8 mm to add a boss.

Like a peg: model a Ø3 × 4 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. Like a bookend: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. Model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (2) Add a Ø12 mm boss, 14 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M12 × 1.75 external thread over its full length, with a 1.75 mm chamfer at the tip. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 1 mm.

Like a O-ring seat: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 0.96 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with a variable radius: 1.1 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 2.2 mm at the opposite point.

Like a peg: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a 4.8 × 4.8 mm square notch, 20 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Sketch a 1.6 × 1.6 mm square whose centre is 6 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face.

Like a tile: model a 2400 × 1600 × 1000 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 190 × 190 mm square pad, 190 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1040 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Make a separate sphere of Ø2260 mm centred on the body's bounding-box centre, and keep only the intersection of the body with it. (3) Hollow the body to 96 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. (1) Cut a 0.48 × 0.48 mm square notch, 0.5 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (2) Hollow the body to 0.2 mm walls, removing the top face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.2 mm.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3000 mm, tube Ø800 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with a constant 56 mm radius. (2) Hollow the body to 48 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. Like a ball: model a sphere of Ø4 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 1.2 mm, leaving a flat of Ø3.2 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (2) Loft a neck 1.3 mm tall from a 0.32 × 0.32 mm square sketched at the centre of the flat cap face to a Ø0.32 mm circle on a plane 1.3 mm above it. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with 0.16 mm.

(3) Add a Ø100 mm boss, 120 mm tall, at the centre of the top face and model an M100 × 6 external thread over its full length, with a 6 mm chamfer at the tip.

(2) Add a 2 × 2 mm square boss, 8 mm tall, centred 3 mm from the centre of the top face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre.

Like a hoop: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. Make a separate Ø0.24 mm cylinder, 0.96 mm long, lying along the Y axis with its axis 0.06 mm below the flat cut face at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0), and subtract it from the body.

Like a finial: model a sphere of Ø4 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 1.2 mm, leaving a flat of Ø3.2 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Hollow the body to 0.19 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Drill a Ø0.38 mm blind hole, 1.6 mm deep, in the flat cap face with its centre 1.4 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so only a 0.01 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Split the body with the plane Z = -0.4 mm into two bodies and keep both.

Model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add two Ø4.8 mm cylinders, 4.8 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 26 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and exactly 4.8 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (2) Cut a Ø4 mm hole 10 mm deep, centred 6 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis.

Like a key fob: model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Cut a Ø130 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 400 mm deep. (2) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 64 mm.

Like a nozzle: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (3) Draft all side faces by 3°, with the bottom face as the neutral plane, so the body narrows toward the top face.

Like a bead: model a sphere of Ø1000 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 499.99975 mm, which is 0.00025 mm below the pole and leaves a flat of Ø1 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the flat cap face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Chamfer the outer edge loop of the flat cap face with an unequal chamfer, 0.05 mm down the side and 0.1 mm across the face.

brief: Model a sphere of Ø4 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 1.2 mm, leaving a flat of Ø3.2 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (2) Cut a Ø0.38 mm notch, 1.6 mm deep, centred exactly on the outer edge of the flat cap face at the sphere's 0° meridian seam (at +X), so it straddles the seam. (3) Extrude a Ø0.32 mm circle sketched at the centre of the flat cap face upward 1.3 mm to add a boss.

Like a leaf: model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. Model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. Like a bangle: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (3) Extrude a Ø0.12 mm circle sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) upward 0.24 mm to add a boss.

Like a peg: model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. Like a knob blank: model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (2) Sweep a Ø0.12 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 0.36 mm that leaves the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Add a Ø0.24 mm boss, 0.24 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.88 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Cut a Ø0.2 mm hole 0.8 mm deep, centred 0.3 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, then repeat it 6 times in a circular pattern about that axis.

Like a finial: model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Add a Ø4.8 mm boss, 4.8 mm tall, on the flat cap face with its centre 17.6 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Cut a Ø4 mm hole at the centre of the flat cap face, 16 mm deep. (3) Hollow the body to 2.4 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed).
Like a panel: model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.4 mm deep.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø50 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø20 mm at the top, 50 mm tall. (1) Cut a Ø2.4 mm notch, 10 mm deep, centred exactly on the outer edge of the top face at the cone's 0° seam line (at +X), so it straddles the seam. (2) Sketch a 0.8 × 0.8 mm square whose centre is 3 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 1 mm.

Like a O-ring seat: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.8 mm. (2) Add a 1.9 × 1.9 mm square pad, 1.9 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (3) Extrude a Ø1.6 mm circle sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) upward 3.2 mm to add a boss.

Like a cam: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. Model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (2) Cut a 0.29 × 0.29 mm square notch, 1 mm deep, with its centre exactly on the outer edge of the top face at +Y (the notch corners turn the edge chain). (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with a variable radius: 0.17 mm at the +X point, rising linearly to 0.34 mm at the opposite point.

(2) Fillet both edge loops (inner and outer circle) of the flat cut face with 0.8 mm.

Like a panel: model a 60 × 40 × 25 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. Sketch a 1.6 × 1.6 mm square whose centre is 6 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a traffic cone: model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø4 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø2 mm at the top, 3 mm tall. (1) Hollow the body to 0.12 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Cut a Ø0.24 mm notch, 1 mm deep, centred exactly on the outer edge of the top face at the cone's 0° seam line (at +X), so it straddles the seam. (3) Loft a neck 0.8 mm tall from a 0.2 × 0.2 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.2 mm circle on a plane 0.8 mm above it.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. (1) Hollow the body to 48 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add two Ø96 mm cylinders, 96 mm tall, standing on the top face with centres 320 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X and exactly 96 mm apart in Y, so they touch along a single vertical line while both fuse to the face (the body touches itself there). (3) Cut a Ø80 mm hole 320 mm deep at the centre of the top face, then repeat it 4 times, 120 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the top face that curves toward +Y with a 480 mm radius.

Model a sphere of Ø2400 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 720 mm, leaving a flat of Ø1920 mm; the body is the part below that plane. (1) Hollow the body to 120 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a 190 × 190 mm square boss, 770 mm tall, centred 285 mm from the centre of the flat cap face toward +Y, then mirror it across the XZ plane through the face centre.

Like a pebble: model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. (1) Add a Ø0.29 mm boss, 0.29 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1.855 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Cut a Ø0.24 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.8 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 0.36 mm pitch (centred on the hole).

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø50 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø20 mm at the top, 50 mm tall. Sketch a 0.8 × 0.8 mm square whose centre is 3 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face.

Model a sphere of Ø50 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 15 mm, leaving a flat of Ø40 mm; the body is the part below that plane. Sweep a Ø4 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 12 mm that leaves the centre of the flat cap face going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube.

Like a tile: model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø0.36 mm boss, 0.36 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 1.82 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Cut a Ø0.3 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 0.8 mm deep. (3) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.15 mm.

Like a spacer block: model a 4 × 3 × 2 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a separate Ø0.36 mm cylinder body, 0.36 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.3 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (2) Loft a neck 0.8 mm tall from a 0.3 × 0.3 mm square sketched at the centre of the top face to a Ø0.3 mm circle on a plane 0.8 mm above it.

Like a donut: model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 0.96 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a 1.9 × 1.9 mm square pad, 1.9 mm tall, on the flat cut face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Sweep a Ø1.6 mm circle along a 90° arc of radius 4.8 mm that leaves the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) going straight up and ends heading toward +Y, to add a bent tube.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø50 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø20 mm at the top, 50 mm tall. (1) Hollow the body to 1.2 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a separate Ø2.4 mm cylinder body, 2.4 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 2 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Cut a Ø2 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 8 mm deep, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 3 mm pitch (centred on the hole).

Model a sphere of Ø4 mm centred on the origin, with the top removed by the plane Z = 1.2 mm, leaving a flat of Ø3.2 mm; the body is the part below that plane. brief: Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø1000 mm, tube Ø1 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø60 mm, tube Ø16 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (2) Hollow the body to 0.8 mm walls, removing the flat cut face. (3) Cut a Ø1.6 mm hole, 3.2 mm deep, in the flat cut face 6.4 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 30 mm, Y = 0) toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 2.4 mm pitch.

Like a peg: model a Ø40 × 60 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Cut a Ø4 mm hole, 16 mm deep, in the top face 16 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 6 mm pitch. (2) Drill a Ø4.8 mm blind hole, 20 mm deep, in the top face with its centre 17.58 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, so only a 0.02 mm wall remains between the hole and the outer edge. (3) Sketch a 1.6 × 1.6 mm square whose centre is 6 mm from the vertical axis through the centre of the top face, and revolve it 360° about that axis to cut a ring groove into the top face.

Model a 1000 × 200 × 1 mm block, centred on the origin and resting on Z = 0. (1) Hollow the body to 0.24 mm walls leaving a closed internal void (no face removed). (2) Add a separate Ø0.48 mm cylinder body, 0.48 mm tall, standing on Z = 0 with its nearest side 0.4 mm outside the body toward +X, and do not merge it. (3) Cut a Ø0.4 mm hole 0.4 mm deep at the centre of the top face, then repeat it 4 times, 0.6 mm apart measured along a path, following an arc in the top face that curves toward +Y with a 2.4 mm radius.

Model a Ø1200 × 2400 mm cylinder with a vertical axis through the origin, resting on Z = 0. (1) Add a 140 × 140 mm square pad, 140 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 480 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (2) Cut a Ø120 mm hole at the centre of the top face, 480 mm deep.

Model the upper half (Z ≥ 0) of a torus about the Z axis: centre-circle Ø3.6 mm, tube Ø1.2 mm, cut by the plane Z = 0, so the body has a flat annular face at Z = 0. (1) Add a Ø0.14 mm boss, 0.14 mm tall, on the flat cut face with its centre 0.53 mm from the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) toward +X, so its side is exactly tangent to the face's outer edge. (2) Extrude a Ø0.12 mm circle sketched at the point on the centre circle of the flat cut face at +X (X = 1.8 mm, Y = 0) upward 0.24 mm to add a boss.

Like a guitar pick: model a 1000 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (1200, 0), (909, 606), (0, 720), (-909, 606), (-1200, 0), (-789, -526), (-0, -880), (789, -526)]. (1) Cut a Ø130 mm hole, 400 mm deep, in the top face 1072 mm from the centre of the top face toward -X, then repeat it in a linear pattern of 3 along Y at 190 mm pitch. (2) Add a 150 × 150 mm square pad, 150 mm tall, on the top face, rotated 45° about the vertical axis, with its +X corner vertex exactly on the face's outer edge at the +X point. (3) Extrude a Ø130 mm circle sketched at the centre of the top face upward 400 mm to add a boss.

Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø6 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø1 mm at the top, 1000 mm tall. (1) Fillet the outer edge loop of the top face with 0.05 mm. (2) Add a 0.12 × 0.12 mm square pad, 0.12 mm tall, on the top face with its centre 0.4 mm from the centre of the top face toward +X, and a second identical pad directly beside it toward +Y sharing one side face, so the two pad tops are exactly coplanar and the two pads touch face to face. (3) Hollow the body to 0.05 mm walls, removing the top face.

topology: feature at a seam or pole
brief: Like a key fob: model a 2 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (2, 0), (1.51, 1.14), (0, 1.35), (-1.51, 1.14), (-2, 0), (-1.31, -0.986), (-0, -1.65), (1.31, -0.986)]. brief: Model a cone frustum with a vertical axis through the origin, Ø2000 mm at the bottom (Z = 0), Ø800 mm at the top, 2000 mm tall. (3) Make a separate Ø160 mm sphere centred on the top face at the centre of the top face and join it to the body.

Like a paddle: model a 1 mm tall extrusion, from Z = 0, of a closed spline outline (see below) [a closed periodic cubic spline through the points (X, Y) mm: (500, 0), (379, 75.7), (0, 90), (-379, 75.7), (-500, 0), (-329, -65.7), (-0, -110), (329, -65.7)]. Hollow the body to 0.2 mm walls, removing the top face.
